sources.title: Response to Scott: selected continuation on page853
sources.citation: Linda Gordon, “Response to Scott,” Signs15(4), Summer1990,852–853, doi:10.1086/494632. Selectedp853 continuation reproduced in the publisher’s first-page image for the following review, doi:10.1086/494633.

verification.note: Fresh visual reading of publisher image494633.fp.png, printedp853, beginning with continuation of Gordon’s response and ending at the next review heading. Gordon defends agency arising through unequal parties’ conflicts and distinguishes violence from representations while retaining social-control analysis. Page852, the later853–858review and Scott’s859–860response remain unread; Crossref confirms separate item identities and pagination. This is a partial primary witness, not the complete exchange.

sources.title: Child Abuse, Gender, and the Myth of Family Independence
sources.citation: Linda Gordon, “Child Abuse, Gender, and the Myth of Family Independence: Thoughts on the History of Family Violence and Its Social Control1880–1920,” Review of Law & Social Change12(1983–84),523–538.

verification.note: Fresh selected primary reading: opening523–524, social-control argument529–534 and concluding536–537; finalPDFleaf538isblank. Boston child-protection case records support a history of negotiated intervention and unequal interests within families. The article retains the explanatory value of social control while criticizing one-way accounts and an imagined formerly autonomous family. Lasch, Parsons/Bales, Piven/Cloward and Ehrenreich/English are explicitly discussed; cited original books unread. Upload2017 is not publication date. The whole subsequent1988monograph was not read.

hc176_linda_gordon_1.note: Fresh selected rereading 2026-10-28: Goodman’s HNN profile, dated12November2006, reproduces Gordon’s own Personal Anecdote, where she expressly credits Alice Clark’s1919book with her material understanding of gender. The personal recollection distinguishes her earlier Russian-history training and1969feminist organizing. Her reproduced Difference excerpts credit Marcuse and C.Wright Mills; the2000movement keynote uses Charles Payne. None has an existing individual graph endpoint. Reproduced Fass/Lassonde reviews retain named mediation; complete monographs remain unread. The paired1991/1999Difference attribution is not collated against either original edition.
